reason: Relocating a section legitimately renames its heading, and re-wrapping a moved paragraph legitimately changes where its lines break. Both make an exact-line comparison report a loss that is not one. Every allowance is recorded here rather than passed on a command line, so a reviewer sees the full list without having to reproduce the failing run — and every entry naming `survivesAs` is checked by the tool, not taken on trust. Two entries are deliberate DELETIONS. ONE of them is a `delete-and-link` under the classification table's disposition — it is marked `deletedAndLinkedTo` and the tool verifies a live link to the owner exists, so a deletion can never be filed as if it were a rename. The OTHER (entry 12) was reclassified in round 4 as an in-package duplicate of a boundary this SPEC already stated, so it carries no owner and no link; it rests on its written reason. The tool's stdout is the authority on these counts: `9 rename(s) ... 1 delete-and-link(s) ... 3 on a written reason`.
